attempts.raw_response:
The development varies in height from 3 to 23 storeys negotiating an abrupt shift in urban scale from the Barkantine Estate to the West with the emerging Millennium Quarter to the East. Family-sized units are located at the base of the building having direct access to rear gardens, a playground and communal courtyard areas. Smaller sized units are located higher up in the towers enjoying views across London from roof terraces and balconies.

The material palette draws from the industrial heritage of the Isle of Dogs, utilizing brick and metal cladding to create a contemporary aesthetic that respects its riverside context. The development incorporates sustainable design principles including rainwater harvesting, green roofs and high levels of thermal insulation to achieve Code for Sustainable Homes Level 4. A new public piazza at ground level provides pedestrian connections through the site, while dedicated cycle storage and proximity to Crossrail stations encourage sustainable transport choices for future residents.

The development comprises 385 new homes across five distinct buildings, designed to integrate seamlessly with the surrounding regeneration area. The material palette draws from the industrial heritage of the Isle of Dogs, featuring brickwork cladding and aluminium window systems that reflect local architectural character. Ground floor commercial units fronting the main road create active street frontages and support the emerging local economy.

Sustainability measures include photovoltaic panels on roof spaces, rainwater harvesting systems, and high-performance insulation to achieve Code for Sustainable Homes Level 4. The scheme provides 162 affordable housing units distributed throughout the development, with shared equity options available for key workers. A dedicated cycle storage facility encourages sustainable transport, while electric vehicle charging points serve the 245 car parking spaces provided at podium level. The project was delivered in three phases between 2018 and 2022.

pair.human_continuation:
A community space was designed as an integral part of the project and incorporates a rooftop sports pitch. The development makes use of a local 'Combined Heat and Power' system and includes greenwalls, bird boxes, bat boxes, insect bricks and biodiversity roofs to help develop local eco-systems. The distinctive skyline and elevations of the building include coloured fibre cement cladding panels, large overhanging canopies and projecting balconies which contrast with the restrained aesthetic of Canary Wharf. Piers Gough described the development as 'humanist architecture of raw funky collage'.

The project was designed by Brady Mallalieu Architects and was developed by the Irish property firm Ballymore. The social and shared ownership housing was managed by the housing association One Housing which subsequently acquired the freehold in 2016.
